Pacanow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pacanów, Poland

Demolished. Pacanów's Jewish settlement dates to the 16th century, reaching 1,689 people (65 percent of the town) by 1921, most murdered by the Germans at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, likely founded in the second half of the 17th century, received victims of the ghetto period, including about 60 people murdered in October 1942; a 1960 closure order described it as already reduced to pastureland, with valuable tombstones destroyed during the occupation. A fire station was later built on the site. In 2020, at the initiative of students from the local Kornel Makuszyński Primary School and Henryk Góra, a new monument and fenced lapidarium were established using recovered tombstones.
